newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-St Barbara plans Mt Leyshon merger.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-St Barbara plans Mt Leyshon merger.

text.p: Perth-based St Barbara Mines Ltd said on Wednesday that it proposed to merge with fellow gold miner Mt Leyshon Gold Mines Ltd.
St Barbara said the offer would be 32 of its shares for each 10 Mt Leyshon shares. It said Mt Leyshon had indicated in preliminary discussions that it was receptive to an offer.
St Barbara said the merger would create a significant Australian gold company with annual gold production of about 350,000 ounces and a resource base of about 4.8 million ounces.
Mt Leyshon is about 75 percent owned by Normandy Mining Ltd.
At St Barbara's closing share price of 80 cents on Tuesday, the offer represented a 22 percent premium to the last sale price for Mt Leyshon of A$2.10 on the same day, St Barbara said.
St Barbara chairman Peter Jones said the two companies, which each have a market capitalisation of about A$165 million, appeared to complement each other.
"Both are currently significant gold producers in their own right," he said in a statement.
"However, St Barbara also brings to the merger a substantial exploration portfolio and development opportunities, whereas Mt Leyshon also brings strong cashflow and financial strength."
St Barbara said Normandy would become its largest shareholder, with 41.3 percent, if the merger was successful.
Mt Leyshon's primary asset is its Mt Leyshon mine near Charters Towers in Queensland, which produced 210,704 ounces of gold in the year to June 30, 1996.
St Barbara's main asset is its Bluebird operation near Meekatharra in Western Australia which produced 118,588 ounces of gold during the same period.
St Barbara shares closed on Wednesady two cents lower at 78 cents while Mt Leyshon was two cents stronger at A$2.12.
The announcement was made after the close of trade.
